summary: Half-Life franchise entries added as supplemental sourced guide rows; Sami did not list these in the locked personal spine.

entries.title: Half-Life

emulation.notes: Native Windows is primary. PCSX2 only applies to the separate Decay/PS2 route.

primary.why: The 25th Anniversary Steam build is Valve's current supported route for the original Half-Life, with restored bonus content and modern compatibility work. It supports Windows, OS X, and Linux, while the PlayStation 2 port is kept separate from the Decay entry because Decay is cataloged as its own game.
primary.how_to_play: Use the current Steam Windows build of Half-Life. Use the PlayStation 2 version only for comparison, and play Decay through its own entry.

entries.remaster_caveats: Half-Life: Source is not the preferred route after the 25th Anniversary update; use it only for Source-engine comparison or mod dependencies.

entries.title: Half-Life: Uplink

emulation.notes: Native Windows through Half-Life on Steam.

primary.version: Half-Life 25th Anniversary Steam build bonus content
primary.why: Half-Life: Uplink was a standalone demo/mini-campaign and is included as restored bonus content in Valve's 25th Anniversary route for Half-Life.
primary.how_to_play: Launch the Uplink bonus content from the current Steam Half-Life install rather than hunting for the old standalone demo.

entries.remaster_caveats: Treat Uplink as bonus/demo content rather than a full sequel.

primary.why: Opposing Force is a Gearbox-developed Half-Life expansion released for Windows and later Steam-supported OS X/Linux routes. Windows Steam is the safest high-fidelity capture path.
primary.how_to_play: Use the current Steam Windows version, keeping the Half-Life base install current.

entries.title: Half-Life: Blue Shift

primary.version: Steam version with High Definition Pack option
primary.why: Blue Shift began as Dreamcast-related content but released as a standalone Windows game, later reaching OS X and Linux through Steam. Windows Steam is the primary capture route and includes the High Definition Pack path.
primary.how_to_play: Use the current Steam Windows build. Decide before capture whether to enable or avoid the High Definition Pack for presentation consistency.

entries.remaster_caveats: The High Definition Pack changes presentation; choose consistently before capture.

entries.title: Half-Life: Decay

emulation.notes: Use accurate PS2 emulation with two controllers, or original hardware for authenticity.

primary.version: Half-Life PS2 Decay campaign via PCSX2 or original hardware
primary.why: Decay is documented as a PlayStation 2-exclusive cooperative expansion bundled with the PS2 version of Half-Life. Because no official PC release is sourced, the archive route is PS2 via accurate emulation or original hardware.
primary.how_to_play: Use a legally owned PlayStation 2 copy of Half-Life in PCSX2 with two-controller setup, or original PS2 hardware, and play only the Decay campaign.

entries.remaster_caveats: Do not substitute unofficial PC ports for the primary archive route unless a later official release appears.

entries.title: Half-Life 2

emulation.notes: Native Windows. Console emulation is unnecessary for the researched route.

primary.why: Valve's 20th Anniversary Update adds fixes, commentary, Workshop support, Episode One, Episode Two, and Lost Coast access from the Half-Life 2 client. For the base Half-Life 2 campaign, Windows is the highest-fidelity and most complete current route.
primary.how_to_play: Use the current Steam Windows build of Half-Life 2. Play the base campaign from the main menu, then use the linked entries for Episode One, Episode Two, and Lost Coast.

entries.remaster_caveats: The anniversary build changes and fixes presentation details; use the current build unless a preservation run specifically requires the 2004 release behavior.

entries.title: Half-Life 2: Deathmatch

primary.why: Half-Life 2: Deathmatch is a standalone multiplayer Half-Life series release on Windows, Mac OS X, and Linux. Windows Steam is the default preservation route for the active PC multiplayer build.
primary.how_to_play: Use the Steam Windows build and document multiplayer availability separately from the single-player Half-Life 2 route.

entries.remaster_caveats: Multiplayer availability depends on current servers/community activity.

entries.title: Half-Life 2: Lost Coast

primary.why: Lost Coast is a free Half-Life 2 additional level and HDR tech demo. Valve's 20th Anniversary Half-Life 2 route adds Lost Coast to the Extras menu, making the current Windows Half-Life 2 client the cleanest route.
primary.how_to_play: Launch Lost Coast from the Half-Life 2 Extras menu in the current Steam Windows build.

entries.remaster_caveats: Lost Coast is a short HDR tech-demo level, not a full sequel.

entries.title: Half-Life Deathmatch: Source

primary.why: Half-Life Deathmatch: Source is the Source-engine multiplayer version of Half-Life deathmatch, available through Steam on PC platforms. Windows is the default capture and compatibility route.
primary.how_to_play: Use the current Steam Windows build and treat it as a multiplayer-only preservation entry.

entries.remaster_caveats: Multiplayer-only; preserve separately from the original Half-Life campaign.

entries.title: Half-Life 2: Survivor
entries.definitive_edition: Original Taito Type X+ arcade release

emulation.emulator: Arcade preservation setup if original cabinet is unavailable
emulation.notes: Prefer original hardware; document any preservation setup explicitly.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original Taito Type X+ arcade cabinet

primary.why: Half-Life 2: Survivor is an arcade adaptation released on Taito Type X+ hardware. Because it is a distinct arcade release with cabinet controls and no sourced official home version, the original arcade build is the primary preservation target.
primary.how_to_play: Use an original cabinet or verified arcade-preservation setup only. Do not substitute fan PC ports for the primary route.

entries.remaster_caveats: Network features and arcade availability may be preservation blockers; avoid unsourced fan ports as the official route.

entries.title: Half-Life 2: Episode One

primary.why: Episode One originally released as a standalone PC episode and later appeared in The Orange Box and other PC routes. Valve's 20th Anniversary Half-Life 2 update now makes Episode One playable from the Half-Life 2 main menu, so Windows is the best current complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Use the current Steam Windows build of Half-Life 2 and launch Episode One from the main menu.

entries.remaster_caveats: Standalone legacy app may remain useful for old mods, but the integrated Half-Life 2 route is the current play route.

entries.title: Half-Life 2: Episode Two

primary.why: Episode Two was part of The Orange Box and later PC platform routes. Valve's 20th Anniversary Half-Life 2 update integrates Episode Two into the Half-Life 2 main menu, making Windows the best current complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Use the current Steam Windows build of Half-Life 2 and launch Episode Two from the main menu.

entries.remaster_caveats: Standalone legacy app may remain useful for old mods, but the integrated Half-Life 2 route is the current play route.

entries.title: Half-Life: Alyx

emulation.notes: Native PC VR. Headset and GPU choice define the fidelity ceiling.

primary.why: Half-Life: Alyx is Valve's VR Half-Life game for Windows and Linux with support for SteamVR-compatible headsets. Windows PC VR has the broadest headset/GPU capture route and highest practical fidelity ceiling.
primary.how_to_play: Use the Steam Windows build with a high-end SteamVR-compatible headset and GPU. Tune headset resolution, refresh rate, and capture settings before recording.

entries.remaster_caveats: Requires VR hardware; non-VR mods are not the primary route for a first archive playthrough.

entries.title: Black Mesa

primary.why: Black Mesa is a standalone third-party remake of Half-Life, approved for commercial release by Valve and fully released for Windows and Linux. Windows is the highest-fidelity capture route, while the original Half-Life remains its own entry because this is a remake rather than a replacement for preservation.
primary.how_to_play: Use the Steam Windows build as a separate remake playthrough after the original Half-Life route, not as a substitute for the 1998 game.

entries.remaster_caveats: This is a remake by Crowbar Collective, not the original Valve game; do not conflate it with the original Half-Life entry.
